condensed_reasoning:
## Research

I set out to identify the last IBRiS/Rzeczpospolita "gdyby wybory do Sejmu" poll published on or before 7 Aug 2026 and compute KO's lead over PiS. My starting brief carried a premise (late-July KO 30.1 vs PiS 28.7, a +1.4pp lead). My research sub-agent immediately flagged that premise as unverifiable.

I found the resolving poll: **IBRiS for Rzeczpospolita, fieldwork 24–25 July 2026** (CATI, n=1,000, published ~27 July). Every outlet — `rp.pl`, `GazetaPrawna`, `dorzeczy.pl`, `wp.pl` — reported the same sole "gdyby wybory" table: **KO 30.1% / PiS 17.3%**, with Morawiecki's new **Rozwój Plus at 7.4%** listed separately following the PiS split (Kaczyński expelled ~30 members on 24 July). That gives a lead of **+12.8pp**. I confirmed via `fetch_url` on the primary rp.pl article that **only one variant was published** — the fine print explicitly states "the content does not show PiS at 28.7% in any variant."

## Key Evidence

- **Resolving figure as reported:** KO 30.1 − PiS 17.3 = **+12.8pp**, corroborated across four independent outlets.
- **The author's PiS 28.7% premise is a factual error** — a conflation with the separate United Surveys/IPSOS series (~28%). I disregarded it; the open upper bound of the question permits values >10.
- **The ~21.5% "baseline" PiS** (Rozwój Plus reabsorbed) exists **only in the WP/United Surveys-by-IBRiS series**, a different commissioner that the resolution fine print explicitly disregards. No baseline is published in the qualifying rp.pl series.
- **Cadence:** IBRiS/Rz polls roughly monthly (late May → 16–17 Jun → 2–3 Jul → 24–25 Jul). The 24–25 Jul poll was an off-cycle, event-driven addition. The next scheduled poll would fall ~late August — outside the window. I estimated a **~28% chance** a new event-driven IBRiS/Rz poll publishes before Aug 7.

## Conclusion

I ran a mixture Monte Carlo. My first pass placed ~38% of the no-new-poll mass on a "baseline reabsorption" fork (~+6), pulling the median to ~10.5. The **premortem reviewer correctly caught this as a resolver-invalid interpretation** — the criteria say to use the figure "as reported" on rp.pl (17.3), and the only source publishing a baseline is the disregarded commissioner. I removed that fork. The recentered distribution is heavily concentrated at **12.8** (conditional on no new poll, ~72%, the answer is essentially exactly 12.8), with a modest lower tail driven almost entirely by the ~28% new-poll branch (where a fractured right likely still yields an elevated ~9–11 lead, plus a small residual resolver-judgment fork toward ~6). Final: **median ~12.6, P10 ~6.0, P90 ~13.2**, sub-zero (PiS ahead) negligible, open upper bound respected.

capability_gaps: A tool to reliably extract the structured Wikipedia polling table would have let the agent verify the backup resolution path (whether Wikipedia logs PiS at 17.3 vs low-20s), which it flagged as a key what-would-change-my-mind but could not confirm.
subtle_bugs: The rp.pl fetch_url returned 'year not specified in excerpt, but context suggests 2024 based on reference to 2023 election' — a misdating artifact; the agent correctly ignored it since fieldwork dates were confirmed as 2026 elsewhere.

The goniec article slug '080726' could be misread as an 8 July / publication date, but the agent's later notes correctly treated it as a URL identifier describing the same 24-25 July poll, not a distinct newer poll.

classification.approach: Identified the sole reported IBRiS/Rzeczpospolita 24-25 July table (KO 30.1/PiS 17.3=+12.8) as the resolving figure and modeled a mixture Monte Carlo over the ~28% chance of a new pre-Aug-7 poll.
classification.key_uncertainty: Whether a new event-driven IBRiS/Rzeczpospolita poll publishes before Aug 7 (~28%), since without one the answer is mechanically exactly 12.8.

risk_flags.evidence: The agent's OWN first-pass Monte Carlo assigned ~38% of the no-new-poll branch to a 'baseline reabsorption' PiS ~24 fork (lead ~6), which the premortem showed contradicts the resolution criteria ('as reported' = 17.3) and its own fetch_url finding ('Only ONE variant is reported'). This was corrected, but only after the adversarial gate — the initial estimate (median 10.5) was materially miscalibrated.

Even after correction, ~28% new-poll probability plus a residual fork produce a lower tail (P10 6.0) that may be slightly fat: conditional on no new poll the answer is deterministically 12.8, and the ~28% new-poll estimate itself is a soft judgment with no hard scheduling signal, so the wide P1-P30 range (2.9-10.5) rests heavily on one uncertain parameter.

strengths: Caught and corrected a factual error embedded in the question's own premise (PiS 28.7%/+1.4pp), tracing it to a conflation with the separate United Surveys/IPSOS series rather than anchoring to it.

Rigorously distinguished the qualifying rp.pl IBRiS series from the disregarded United Surveys-by-IBRiS (WP) and Polsat News series — the crux of correct resolution, since the WP series was the only source of the tempting ~21.5% baseline PiS.
Verified the resolving figure across four independent outlets and used fetch_url on the primary rp.pl article to confirm only ONE variant (with Rozwój Plus split out) was published.
Explicitly checked that no August 2026 IBRiS/Rz poll existed yet, confirming 24-25 July as the resolving poll.
Responded correctly to the premortem: removed the resolver-invalid baseline fork and recentered from median 10.5 to 12.6 with documented, re-run Monte Carlo percentiles.
weaknesses: The initial Monte Carlo over-weighted a resolver-invalid 'baseline reabsorption' fork despite the agent's own findings file conceding 'rp.pl article ONLY presented the 17.3 scenario -> strongly favors +12.8' — an internal contradiction that required the premortem to resolve.

The ~28% new-poll probability is asserted from cadence reasoning but never stress-tested against a concrete signal (e.g., whether IBRiS pre-announced a follow-up), leaving the entire lower tail resting on one soft parameter.

Did not probe whether Wikipedia would log the poll with a low-20s baseline PiS (a plausible resolver backup path) beyond a single fetch that returned only the article intro — the Wikipedia table was never actually extracted.

issues: Two asknews tools (search_news, do_news_research) returned 403 Forbidden due to plan-tier restrictions — minor wasted calls but no impact since search/research/fetch_url covered the need.
ToolSearch returned empty results twice, adding no value.

The parent trace file exceeded the read tool's size/token limits (345KB / 26k tokens), and the premortem sub-agent's trace_at_premortem.md hit a 102k-token read cap, forcing Grep-based navigation — a minor friction, not a forecast-affecting issue.

evidence: Question dated on/around 2026-07-27; resolving poll (fieldwork 24-25 July, published ~27 July) falls at the start of the window and was legitimately available.
The agent explicitly searched for and confirmed no August 2026 IBRiS/Rz poll existed as of 27 July, rather than assuming a future result.
All sources accessed carry accessed_at 2026-07-27; no post-cutoff information was used. This is effectively a live forecast, not a retrodict.

actionable_improvements: Down-weight resolver-interpretation forks that contradict the criteria BEFORE the premortem gate — the agent's own findings file already noted 'rp.pl ONLY presented the 17.3 scenario,' so the baseline fork should never have received 38% weight in the first Monte Carlo.
Stress-test the single dominant free parameter (the ~28% new-poll probability) with an explicit sensitivity band, since the entire lower tail depends on it.
When a backup resolution source (Wikipedia) is cited as a what-would-change-my-mind, extract its actual table rather than settling for the article intro.
